name: Insertion Sort
summary: Builds the sorted array one element at a time by inserting each element into its place among the ones before it.
description: Insertion Sort works the way many people sort playing cards in their hand. The left part of the array is always sorted. In every step the next element (the key) is taken out, and each bigger element of the sorted part is shifted one position to the right to make room for it.
As soon as an element that is not bigger than the key is found, or the start of the array is reached, the key is placed into the gap that was left behind.

On nearly sorted data Insertion Sort is very fast, close to O(n), because only a few elements have to be shifted. That is why fast hybrid algorithms such as Timsort use it for small pieces of an array. On random or reversed data it needs O(n²) time.
